ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all identified shareholders, directors, beneficiaries, and source-of-funds counterparties against the United Nations Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, HMT UK Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit domestic watchlist. PEP status must be disclosed on the UBO Declaration and triggers enhanced due diligence, independent verification of source of wealth, and senior-management approval prior to company formation. Screening must be repeated at least quarterly for as long as the International Company remains active.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Companies Registry administered by the Samoa International Financial Services Centre
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: International Company names may be registered in English, Samoan, or a foreign script provided the foreign-script name is accompanied by a certified English or Samoan transliteration acceptable to the Registrar. The statutory suffix must appear in roman letters. Chinese-character names are permitted in the company's constitutional documentation but the registered name shown on the Certificate of Incorporation must include a romanized transliteration for official indexing. Names must not be misleading, identical, or confusingly similar to an existing registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant or licensed registered agent must file a written request for reconsideration with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 calendar days, citing the ground of objection and the proposed remediation. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, a formal administrative appeal may be lodged with the Samoan Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 30 calendar days. A further appeal lies to the Supreme Court of Samoa on a question of law under the Civil Procedure Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible for administrative and correspondence purposes, but the International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa at the premises of its licensed registered agent. The registered agent is statutorily required to hold the company records, UBO register, and minutes at that office. No local staff or physical trading infrastructure is required for the low-risk wholesale asphalt logistics trading model.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for the stated industry; estimated probability of unannounced physical inspection below 5% absent AML/CFT red flags. The likelihood rises to approximately 15% if a shareholder or authorized signatory is classified as a politically exposed person or appears on a sanctions-related watchlist.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Sections 5, 7, 30, 35, 80); Companies Act 2001 (as a contextual reference for non-exempt domestic companies)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), administered through the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation on Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company) together with Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the International Companies Act 1987; the company may be incorporated with a nominal share capital determined by the subscriber, and no escrow or paid-up deposit is required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers having signed the Memorandum and Articles of Association, the shares allotted to the initial subscribers as set out in the register of members are hereby ratified, accepted, and recorded. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the company in Samoa shall be the office of the licensed registered agent as stated in the application for incorporation, and that such address shall be the company's official domicile for service of process. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name], [Name], and [Name] are appointed as the first directors, and [Name] is appointed as company secretary, each having consented to act, with authority to open bank accounts and execute all documents necessary to carry on the company's business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Availability Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA / Registrar of International Companies, MCIL
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application via a licensed registered agent. The proposed name must not be identical or deceptively similar to any existing domestic or international company in Samoa. Provide two alternative names. A certificate of name availability is issued upon approval.
required_dossiers: Proof of residential or business address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit a written request for reconsideration with a fresh alternative name list; the Registrar must provide reasons, and amendment of the application can be made without additional fee if filed within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public / Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association, including the authorized share capital, shareholder restrictions, and director powers. Each subscriber must sign in the presence of a notary public or other person authorized by law. The registered agent countersigns to confirm compliance with the International Companies Act 1987.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any document is defective, the registered agent will file an amended copy with a corrective declaration; resubmission is processed as a continuation of the original application to avoid loss of priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL through SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form IC-1 together with the executed constitutional documents, consent of directors and secretary, registered office confirmation, and the prescribed government fee. The fee can be paid via bank transfer or SIFA-approved electronic payment. The Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director(s) and secretary
Registered office and registered agent confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, the registered agent may submit an amended Form IC-1 with explanatory correspondence; a fresh submission is only required if the defect is substantive (e.g., unlawful object clause). Reconsideration is free of charge if filed within 10 business days of the adverse notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of First Board Resolution and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the board of directors in accordance with Article 2 of the Articles of Association. Adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, ratify the share allotment, adopt the registered office location, and appoint officers. Minutes are signed and maintained in the registered office.
required_dossiers: Register of directors, secretary, and members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the board meeting is challenged for defective notice or quorum, a new meeting may be convened ad hoc; retrospective ratification can be recorded by unanimous written resolution of all directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Regulatory Registration and File Intake
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Revenue (MOR) / Samoa International Finance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Certificate of Incorporation is issued, file for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) with the Ministry of Revenue for non-tax operational filings (e.g., customs, employment). Register with the Samoa National Provident Fund (SNPF) if any employees will be engaged in Samoa, and maintain the required corporate registers at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the TIN application is rejected due to discrepancies, amend the supporting corporate documents and re-file at the MOR; the effective date of registration will remain the date of initial submission if corrected within 14 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) through the Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA); Ministry for the Regulation of Trade and Industry for commercial storage
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Establishment Permit / Operating Permit for Storage and Distribution of Petroleum and Hydrocarbon Products (issued under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004 and Petroleum Act 1984)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA) within the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2: Preliminary Environmental Assessment required for bitumen storage and containerized bulk wholesale facilities; full EIA Report mandatory if storage capacity exceeds 100,000 liters or if the facility is located within 200 meters of a marine protected area, coastline, or residential zone
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero visible oil sheen in stormwater discharges; wastewater pH within 6.0-9.0; total petroleum hydrocarbon (TPH) in discharge not exceeding 10 mg/L; VOC emissions from heated storage tanks must be captured and vented through approved carbon filtration or thermal oxidizer system; hazardous waste shall only be delivered to an MNRE-approved waste contractor

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA), including proof of approved fire suppression systems, emergency exits, fire separation distances, and storage of flammable liquids complying with NFPA 30 standards; structural load inspection from the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (WSTI) to certify elevated storage platforms or mezzanine loading areas; Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) clearance from the Labour Division of MCIL for workplace hazard signage, personnel protective equipment, and operator training records

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), official portal https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned International Company (IC) must engage a licensed local registered agent to incorporate under the International Companies Act 1987 and obtain a Certificate of Incorporation. The registered agent then files an application with the Samoa Revenue Authority through the SRA Taxpayer Registration portal or in person at the SRA headquarters in Apia, submitting the Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association, registered agent confirmation, director and shareholder particulars, and proof of registered office in Samoa. The SRA issues a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and, where relevant, a VAT registration number if the IC opts for voluntary VAT registration. For International Companies recognised under the International Companies Act, the tax identification is administered through the SRA's non-resident taxpayer registry for offshore entities, with the registered agent designated as the filing intermediary.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: International Companies are not subject to Samoa income tax on offshore business income and therefore no check-the-box election is statutorily required for Samoan tax purposes. However, the IC may voluntarily elect to register for Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 1998, as amended, in order to reclaim VAGST on qualifying local inputs or to issue tax invoices for locally consumed supplies. Hybrid mismatch elections are not applicable because Samoa has not adopted OECD hybrid mismatch rules in its domestic International Companies Act, and the IC is an opaque, exempt entity that may nonetheless be treated as a controlled foreign corporation or flow-through entity under the shareholder's home jurisdiction; such foreign classification is governed by foreign law and does not alter the Samoan entity's status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 80,000 per 12-month period for taxable supplies; non-resident and offshore International Companies are outside the scope unless they make taxable supplies in Samoa; voluntary registration is permitted where the SRA deems a taxable activity exists
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: There is currently no mandatory real-time electronic fiscal clearance or digital stamping system for VAGST invoices in Samoa. Taxpayers must issue compliant VAGST tax invoices containing prescribed particulars: supplier name, TIN, invoice serial number, date, recipient details, description of goods, quantity, price, VAGST amount, and total consideration. The SRA is progressively upgrading its electronic filing and taxpayer portal, but no API-based clearance or government-authorised digital fiscal stamp is legally mandated. Customs export documentation is processed through the Samoa Customs Service using the ASYCUDA World electronic customs management system, which provides electronic export declarations and facilitates cross-agency data exchange with the SRA.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Samoa qualify for zero-rating under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act if the goods are physically exported from Samoa within the meaning of the Act, the supplier has evidence of exportation, and the goods are supplied under a contract for sale or exchange where title passes to a person outside Samoa. The zero-rating criterion for a containerized bitumen/asphalt wholesale trading operation requires that the goods are removed from Samoa by the overseas buyer or on behalf of the overseas buyer, through a qualifying customs export declaration. Offshore services supplied to a non-resident recipient outside Samoa are zero-rated where the services are supplied to a person who is not in Samoa at the time of supply and the services are not physically performed in Samoa; however, International Companies engaged in offshore trading activities generally fall outside the VAGST net altogether and do not require a refund claim because they are not registered for VAGST. A registered IC may claim input tax credits or refunds on any VAGST paid on local supplies acquired for the purpose of making zero-rated exports, subject to SRA verification and the filing of a VAGST return for the relevant period.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration submitted electronically via Samoa Customs ASYCUDA World
Bill of Lading (original or certified true copy) in the name of the Samoan exporting entity or its agent
Commercial invoice describing the goods as containerized penetration grade bitumen/asphalt under HS 2713.20 or 2714.90, as applicable
Packing list evidencing container counts and weights
Evidence of payment or inward remittance certificate (or bank SWIFT/TT advice) showing receipt of export proceeds from the overseas buyer
Certificate of origin (if required by the receiving customs jurisdiction)
Copy of the registered agent's or exporter's VAGST registration certificate (only if registered and making zero-rated supplies)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The SRA may conduct a VAT/VAGST audit or customs duty verification and compare export declarations, bills of lading, shipping manifests, and offshore payment records. If an exporter fraudulently zero-rates goods that are not exported, or fails to repatriate export proceeds within the applicable statutory or administrative deadline, the SRA may assess the unpaid VAGST at 15% plus interest, impose penalties under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act (including late payment penalties, evasion penalties, and in serious cases criminal fines), and retrospectively claw back input credits claimed. Claims of fraudulent zero-rating may result in prosecution before the Samoan courts with fines up to the amount prescribed by the Tax Administration Act and imprisonment in aggravated cases. Additionally, the customs authorities may seize or forfeit goods and impose customs penalties for false declarations, and the Financial Intelligence Unit may apply anti-money-laundering penalties where the arrangement discloses proceeds of crime or a fictitious export transaction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), Apia, operating as the consolidated monetary authority and exchange control administrator under the Exchange Control Act 1972 and the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984; day-to-day supervisory control over onshore commercial banks rests with the Banking Supervision Department, while prudential oversight of offshore banks and of the International Company regime is exercised jointly with the Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) and the Registrar of International & Foreign Companies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is a managed-float currency pegged to a composite basket of the currencies of Samoa's principal trading partners. Current-account transactions for bona fide trade in goods are fully convertible through authorized dealers (commercial banks) against documentary proof comprising invoices, packing lists, bills of lading and related payment instructions; bitumen/asphalt imports require no import license, and no product-specific restriction applies to ISIC 4661. The capital account is restricted for resident entities, but Samoa International Companies (ICs) are treated as non-resident for exchange-control purposes; therefore WS_IC may maintain foreign-currency transaction accounts (USD, NZD, AUD, EUR), fund them from any non-resident source, and remit dividends, shareholder-loan principal, and trade settlements without prior Central Bank approval provided all flows are routed through a licensed authorized dealer, correctly narratived, and reported in the dealer's periodic exchange-control returns. If the IC were to transact in WST or receive WST from resident Samoan customers, conversion to foreign currency at the authorized-dealer window would require current-account document verification. The principal profit-repatriation hurdle is not exchange control but compliance documentation: because the IC is tax-exempt under the International Companies Act 1987, no Ministry of Revenue tax clearance is required for dividend remittances, yet the paying bank will demand a board dividend declaration, internally reviewed or audited financial statements, an up-to-date beneficial-ownership register, and a source-of-funds confirmation letter from the directors in order to discharge obligations under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Samoa's exchange-control guidelines require resident exporters to bring export proceeds into Samoa through an authorized dealer within six months of the shipment date; proceeds are normally credited to a prescribed Foreign Currency Account and a mandatory conversion portion (commonly a 50% band per credit, as directed by the Central Bank) must be surrendered into WST unless a standing exemption has been granted. WS_IC, being a non-resident International Company, sits outside the surrender and conversion obligation provided the bitumen sales are invoiced in a foreign currency (USD) and title passes outside Samoa under CIF/FOB destination terms; the IC must nevertheless hold the Central Bank of Samoa's standard non-resident IC foreign-currency classification letter issued through SIFA and must maintain export sales contracts, commercial invoices, bills of lading, and reconciled foreign-currency account statements for inspection by the authorized dealer and SIFA.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Settlement Account (IC current account); separately ring-fenced Capital Escrow Account for shareholder equity injection
Secondary operational WST/USD account and margin account for FX forwards executed at the authorized-dealer window
Offshore USD clearing, LC confirmation, and treasury hedging account (licensed offshore bank under the Central Bank of Samoa)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM, with material legal constraints. Samoa has no electronic-money-institution (EMI) licensing regime; unlicensed overseas digital EMIs (e.g., Wise Business, Airwallex, Currenxie, Mercury) cannot issue a Samoa-domiciled account and generally reject entities lacking a physical presence, local tax ID, or utility bill in the EMI's operating jurisdiction. A Samoa IC may be eligible for a foreign EMI account only if it maintains an operating subsidiary or qualifying proof-of-address in that jurisdiction, and even then the EMI will apply enhanced scrutiny to an offshore/tax-exempt structure, apply lower transaction velocity limits, and may suspend funds pending beneficial-ownership screens. The architecture should therefore treat EMIs exclusively as a secondary collection vehicle for open-account sales in the EU/UK corridor, never as the primary treasury rail; all core inbound and outbound flows must clear through a licensed authorized dealer in Samoa to remain reconcilable with the Exchange Control Act 1972, the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007, and SIFA expectations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is accepted in principle at BSP Samoa and Pacific Commercial Bank for ICs introduced by an SIFA-licensed registered agent, provided the directors are non-PEP individuals and the bank completes a live video identity-verification interview. Required documents for remote opening: authenticated corporate extract from the Registrar of International & Foreign Companies, board resolution approving the account mandate, certified passports and address proofs of each director and signatory, beneficial-ownership declaration, and a registered-agent letter of introduction. In practice, SCB and the BSP capital-escrow team effectively mandate an in-person interview in Apia for at least one executive director or a local company secretary before activation. Recommended protocol: schedule a three-day visit to Apia, hold compliance interviews at BSP and SCB, and appoint a Samoan-resident company secretary or co-signatory isolated from trading operations to preserve a continuous authorized-dealer relationship and to satisfy any residual physical-presence condition.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial-ownership structure of the International Company: the IC Act 1987 allows minimal public filing and legacy bearer shares, creating a shell-company red flag at account inception.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Certificate of Incorporation; Certificate of Good Standing from the Registrar of International & Foreign Companies; updated register of members and directors; Beneficial Ownership Declaration filed under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2018; formal attestation from the licensed Samoa registered agent that no bearer shares are outstanding or, if issued, that the bearer certificates are immobilized and deposited with the agent; source-of-wealth statements for each ultimate beneficial owner; bank reference letters from the shareholder's home jurisdiction; and written confirmation of the IC's non-resident classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Hydrocarbon-sector scrutiny: wholesale bitumen trading into high-risk corridors (Nigeria, West Africa, UAE brokers, China procurement) triggers enhanced due diligence on counterparties, sanctions exposure, and pricing integrity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade-file integrity pack: executed master sales agreement with Incoterms (CIF/FOB); proforma and final commercial invoices; stamped packing lists; full set of ocean bills of lading with HS codes 2713.20.00 or 2715.00; certificate of origin; third-party inspection certificates (SGS, Intertek, or Cotecna); vessel/container screening confirmation against OFAC, EU, UN, and UK sanctions lists; buyer beneficial-owner passports; buyer sanctions-exclusion and end-use attestation; and a market-based pricing matrix (USGC or Brent-derived benchmark) demonstrating arm's-length pricing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-haven/conduit perception: the entity is domiciled in a tax-exempt offshore regime and may be treated as a pure payment-pass-through without economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Economic-substance file: lease agreement for the registered office in Apia; company-secretary and treasury-administration services agreement; board minutes evidencing Samoan-level decisions on banking relationships, FX policy, and trade approvals; current SIFA annual-fee receipts; group audited consolidated accounts showing WS_IC retains genuine gross margin from bitumen resale; and the IC's planned annual attestation filing to SIFA confirming no Samoan-resident business operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction-velocity and corridor red flags: recurring large wires (USD 0.5–2 million per shipment) to/from Nigeria, UAE, and China trip automated monitoring scenarios for fast movement and high-risk geography.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-approval compliance pack maintained with the bank: an approved counterparty list and country-policy matrix; sample SWIFT MT103 narrative format, for example 'LC/INV REF [number] / BITUMEN / HS 2713'; a shipping-cycle diary linking each wire to an LC number and bill-of-lading date; FX forward schedule and hedge-rationale memo; monthly reconciliation statements for the USD account; and a standing arrangement with the compliance officer to receive 24-hour advance notice on wires exceeding USD 1 million.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial equity and shareholder loans must be remitted to WS_IC's BSP Samoa USD account from the parent/shareholder bank outside Samoa (e.g., Singapore, Hong Kong, EU, UAE) via SWIFT MT103 using a direct-investment purpose narrative; field 70 must carry a wording such as 'INV/LOAN – WS_IC – SHAREHOLDER CAPITAL INJECTION – BITUMEN TRADING'. The receiving authorized dealer completes the Central Bank of Samoa's exchange-control declaration form for any single inward credit equivalent to WST 500,000 or more. Verification by the bank comprises the corporate extract, board resolution approving the capital injection and signatory mandate, shareholder register, source-of-funds evidence from the remitting bank, registered-agent confirmation of beneficial owners, and, for a shareholder loan exceeding USD 2,000,000, a signed facility deed with an arm's-length interest rate. The SWIFT GPI tracking reference and the full MT103 copy must be archived for AML audit; no prior Central Bank approval is required for non-resident IC capital injections, but equity versus debt must be clearly labelled in the corporate records to prevent future attribution and thin-capitalization challenges.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rails are (1) irrevocable documentary Letters of Credit opened by buyer banks in Nigeria/UAE/Asia under UCP 600, transmitted via SWIFT MT700/MT707 (MT710 where the issuing bank is not a member), and confirmed at BSP Samoa or Pacific Commercial Bank; the IC presents the full documentary set under the LC and is paid upon compliance through the USD nostro via CHIPS/Fedwire. (2) Direct telegraphic transfers for open-account settlements executed as SWIFT MT103 with field 23B 'SSTD' against matched invoices. (3) Pre-export finance, whereby the IC assigns LC proceeds to the financing bank using a SWIFT MT760 guarantee where required. All outbound supplier disbursements for containerized drummed bitumen procurement (China/Hong Kong corridor) are executed as MT103 credits matched to commercial invoices, purchase orders, packing lists, and CRM/ERP settlement records; payments to shell-company accounts are prohibited. For LC-supported sales, the IC should require a confirmed LC with a sight tenor or a maximum 90-day tenor after sight to preserve liquidity and to align with the confirming bank's discounting facility.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (USD/WST, USD/CNY, USD/NZD) executed with BSP Samoa or SCB as authorized dealer, tenor up to 12 months, supported by genuine underlying trade exposure only
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing USD/WST and USD/CNY where deliverable forwards are illiquid; permitted for hedging LC payables and contracted receivables
Cross-currency swaps (USD to CNH, USD to WST) applied to shareholder loan and trade-payable rebalancing
Plain-vanilla EUR/USD and USD/CNY FX options (purchased calls and puts) used to hedge contingent bid/export pricing; written or short option positions are not permitted under the treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Annual License Fee Declaration, International Companies Act 1987
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: annual return and annual license fee are due on or before each incorporation anniversary, with a 30-day lodgment grace period following the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts a 10% surcharge on the unpaid annual license fee; continued non-payment beyond six months triggers a formal default notice and administrative strike-off (dissolution) by the Registrar of International Companies; after strike-off the company's assets vest in the Crown and directors remain personally liable for debts contracted while the company is struck off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Agent's AML/CFT Continuing Due Diligence Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Registered Agent (acting for SIFA and the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At each incorporation anniversary, before the annual return is accepted; immediate notification to the registered agent is required upon any material shareholding or control change during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm beneficial ownership blocks filing of the annual return; the registered agent must report persistent non-confirmation to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit; repeated non-compliance may result in termination of the registered agent relationship, deregistration of the company, and imposition of AML/CFT penalties

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit threshold applies to a standard Samoa International Company; an independent certified audit is required only if (i) members holding at least 10% of voting shares validly requisition one, (ii) the directors resolve to appoint an auditor, or (iii) the Registrar of International Companies so directs under the International Companies Act 1987; financial statements are not required to be publicly lodged
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted in Samoa; books, records, and underlying documentation must present a true and fair view of the company's affairs, be maintained in English, and be producible within a reasonable period (normally not exceeding 48 hours) as required under the International Companies Act 1987

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended) and the SIFA AML/CFT Rules, the licensed registered agent must verify and confirm the ultimate beneficial ownership of the International Company on each annual renewal date; share transfers or changes in ownership and control during the year must be recorded in the Register of Members and notified to the registered agent for updated risk assessment; the annual return to the Registrar must be accompanied by the agent's confirmation that the shareholder register and beneficial ownership records are accurate and current
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Shareholders) - International Companies Act 1987, s.148
Register of Directors - International Companies Act 1987, s.149
Register of Charges - International Companies Act 1987, s.151
Minute Book (minutes of members' and directors' meetings) - International Companies Act 1987, s.154

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 750 - USD 1,200 per annum (licensed registered agent and registered office in Apia, Samoa, including annual return preparation, statutory register upkeep, and government filing coordination)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 6,000 per engagement (optional certified audit by a licensed Samoan auditor, typically required only for financing, disposal, shareholder requisition, or regulatory direction)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for a Samoa International Company (IC) on all worldwide offshore-source income; Samoa's resident corporate headline rate is 25% under the Income Tax Act 2015, with a 15% concessional rate available to qualifying manufacturing, agriculture, fishing, tourism and ICT companies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption from Samoan income tax for ICs incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987, provided income is not derived from domestic Samoa-source business. The IC is also exempt from capital gains tax, stamp duty on its constitutional and transfer instruments, dividend withholding tax, interest withholding tax, and exchange control. The effective permanent cost is the annual government renewal fee plus the licensed registered agent fee.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IC Economic Substance Return under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2019 (No. 17 of 2019); filed electronically by the licensed Samoa registered agent through the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) / Samoa Revenue electronic registry portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the end of the IC's financial year; the financial year ends on 31 December unless the IC's constitution validly elects an alternative year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part A – Entity and registered particulars
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IC name, incorporation number, registered office in Samoa, registered agent licence number, financial year-end, and board composition.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify every non-resident shareholder, the ultimate parent entity and its tax residence; this data powers automatic exchange of information (AEOI/CbCR) tagging.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from each relevant activity; for this scope: distribution and service centre income from wholesale supply of drummed and bagged penetration grade bitumen (ISIC 4661 / NAICS 424720).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the distribution margin and service fee; disclose separately any incidental income from freight, terminal handling, tolling, or storage of asphalt products.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Samoa premises (owned or leased); number of full-time employees physically employed in Samoa; annual operating expenditure incurred in Samoa; board minutes evidencing procurement, pricing, logistics, and contract negotiation decisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain at least one physical office and one senior executive resident in Samoa; hold board meetings in Samoa at least twice per year and document decisions on cargo routing, supplier selection, letter-of-credit terms, and customer credit limits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part D – High-risk intellectual property schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of IP assets, core income-generating activities, and the jurisdiction of development, exploitation, and custody of IP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the IC owns no high-risk IP used solely to generate royalty income; if a brand or logistics software licence exists, file the licence agreement and demonstrate active Samoan management and decision-making over its commercial exploitation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual ESR return attracts an administrative penalty of up to 100 penalty units (WST 10,000; one penalty unit equals WST 100) plus daily default penalties; continued default enables the Registrar to suspend the certificate of compliance, refuse renewal, strike the IC off the register, and initiate spontaneous exchange of the entire file with the ultimate parent's tax authority.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Return and Renewal of an International Company under the International Companies Act 1987; filed by the registered agent through the MCIL Companies Registry online system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before each anniversary of the date of incorporation; a renewal grace period applies, after which escalating late fees accrue by reference to the Registrar's fees regulations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical address in Samoa where process may be served.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provisioned by the licensed registered agent; a post office box alone is impermissible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and licence number of the Samoan trust and company service provider.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The agent must be a licensed entity under Samoa law and is the legal channel for all regulatory filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal names, nationalities, usual residential addresses, and shareholding percentages of all directors and shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nominee directors are permitted, but the registered agent must hold a complete beneficial-owner schedule for AML and UBO record-keeping.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Issued and paid-up capital, number of classes and shares, and a directors' declaration of solvency.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No minimum capital is required; the solvency declaration must be signed on the date of filing and retained for inspection.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late renewal escalates the prescribed fees; an IC in arrears for more than 6 months is struck off the register, property located in Samoa vests in the Crown, and the former officers are barred from incorporating a new Samoa company for 5 years without the Registrar's consent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No Samoan income tax return is required for a wholly exempt offshore IC. If the IC transacts domestic Samoa-source business, it must register for corporate income tax with the Ministry of Revenue and file the annual company income tax return through the e-Services portal (revenue.gov.ws).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with provisional tax instalments where a taxable liability is anticipated
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final return due within 6 months after the end of the income year (31 December for calendar-year filers); provisional tax payable in instalments as directed by the Commissioner of Revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross income from Samoa-source activities; offshore trading income remains within the exempt IC pool.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Domestic sales of bitumen delivered within Samoa are taxable; export sales and pure offshore trading are excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses incurred in producing assessable income, including a fair allocation of agent, logistics, and administrative costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate the cost base between the taxable domestic pool and the exempt offshore pool using documented internal accounting records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 25% of taxable income less provisional payments and final withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Settle by wire to the Samoa Revenue collection account and retain the electronic acknowledgement for the audit file.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: For a taxable IC: late filing penalty of 25% of the assessed tax, monthly statutory interest on unpaid tax, and shortfall penalties ranging from 20% (failure to take reasonable care) to 150% (evasion); fraudulent returns are subject to criminal prosecution and imprisonment of up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — Samoa does not levy withholding tax on dividends paid by an exempt International Company; distributions of offshore profits to non-resident shareholders are made free of any Samoan tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because no Samoan dividend withholding tax arises on IC distributions, treaty relief is generally not required for outbound dividends. For any income stream that is technically subject to Samoan tax (e.g., domestic-source interest or royalties), the non-resident beneficial owner must: (i) obtain a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority; (ii) submit the TRC together with a signed self-assessment of treaty entitlement (Form DT-1) to the Samoan payer or registered agent before the distribution date; (iii) provide a beneficial-ownership declaration; and (iv) retain source documents for 7 years. Samoa's relevant treaty instruments are the DTA with Australia, the DTA with New Zealand, and the Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters; absent a validly filed TRC, the domestic 15% non-resident withholding rate applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory non-resident final withholding rates under the Income Tax Act 2015: 15% on interest and 15% on royalties paid to non-residents. Under the Samoa–Australia DTA, interest may be taxed at up to 10% and royalties at up to 10%; interest paid to an unrelated banking counterparty on a genuine letter-of-credit or trade finance facility sourced from the exempt offshore pool is not subject to Samoan withholding tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa does not maintain a formal Local File or Master File documentation threshold for exempt ICs; however, the Commissioner may adjust intercompany pricing to reflect the arm's-length standard under the Income Tax Act 2015. For economic substance purposes, an IC with gross income from relevant activities exceeding WST 250,000 per annum must file a full Economic Substance Return; ICs at or below that de minimis threshold file a reduced notification only. A bitumen wholesale trading entity (ISIC 4661) above the threshold must document its Samoan value chain, including the fully burdened distribution margin, personnel costs, premises costs, and sampling of comparable independent distribution margins.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP – Comparable Uncontrolled Price for bitumen sales to independent asphalt terminals
Resale Price Method – wholesale distribution margin benchmarking against independent traders
Cost Plus Method – logistics, tolling, and bagging services
TNMM – net margin on procurement and distribution functions
Profit Split – joint procurement, shipping, and risk-sharing arrangements
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2019 requires an IC to satisfy Samoan economic substance where it carries on a 'relevant activity'. Wholesale trading of drummed and bagged penetration grade bitumen falls within the 'distribution and service centre' category. The IC must demonstrate in Samoa: (i) a physical office; (ii) at least one full-time locally resident executive who manages procurement, pricing, invoicing, and logistics; (iii) operating expenditure in Samoa proportionate to the wholesale margin; and (iv) strategic decisions taken by the board at meetings held in Samoa. Pure back-to-back contracting, remote approval chains, and reliance on foreign fulfilment without local decision-making will fail the test, trigger penalties, and expose the structure to spontaneous exchange of information to the ultimate parent's tax jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False Economic Substance Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing an ESR return that conceals the absence of Samoan premises, staff, or board decisions while booking the full wholesale distribution margin through the IC; using the IC as a pass-through payment conduit without any real commercial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2019, a false return is an offence punishable by a fine of up to WST 100,000 plus daily default penalties, revocation of the certificate of compliance, and mandatory spontaneous exchange of information to the ultimate parent jurisdiction; under the tax administration framework, intentional misstatement attracts shortfall penalties of up to 150% of the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Each director who signs or causes a false ESR or income declaration is personally liable to the penalty regime; fraudulent declarations additionally expose directors to criminal prosecution, imprisonment of up to 5 years, disqualification from managing any Samoa company, and civil restitution to the Revenue for the evaded tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the IC as a pure invoice‑pass‑through with a PO Box office, nominee directors without knowledge or authority, no active Samoan bank account, no locally resident personnel, and no verifiable record of procurement, pricing, or logistics decisions in Samoa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The entity is rebuttably presumed to lack the substance required for IC tax-exempt status; the Registrar will decline renewal and strike the company off, and the asset-protection benefit collapses because assets located in Samoa vest in the Crown; the full ownership and financial profile will be exchanged under AEOI/CbCR frameworks to the foreign parent's tax authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors who append signatures without exercising fiduciary oversight face statutory fines and disqualification; beneficial owners using a shell to evade the home jurisdiction face reassessment, GAAR recharacterization, civil recovery, and coordinated enforcement through mutual assistance in tax collection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain complete and current beneficial-ownership records at the registered agent's office; use of bearer shares or opaque nominee layers to conceal the underlying trader; routing open-account or commodity letter-of-credit proceeds through unrelated third-party accounts; structuring cargo settlements below reporting thresholds to evade transaction screening.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Proceedings under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism Act 2018: business-registration suspension, asset-freezing orders issued by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit, fines of up to WST 1,000,000 for the entity together with confiscation, and independent fines against the registered agent for failure to file suspicious activity reports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who conceal the principal, sign false KYC attestations, or knowingly move proceeds of customs fraud on asphalt imports face imprisonment of up to 7 years for money laundering; civil confiscation may reach personal assets, and the court may impose travel bans pending the conclusion of the investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Aggressive Structuring / Treaty and GAAR Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing the bitumen wholesale IC solely to strip commission income out of a foreign group without any change in value-adding functions, without bearing distribution risk, without holding inventory, and without independent capacity to negotiate contracts; applying a zero-tax label to profits economically sourced in a foreign market.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Samoa's participation in the Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance enables spontaneous exchange of ESR, banking, and beneficial-ownership data; the foreign parent's tax authority applies its general anti-avoidance rule and transfer-pricing adjustments, reverses the profits, imposes understatement penalties of up to 100% of the tax avoided, and denies treaty benefits to the conduit IC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the foreign authority pierces the corporate veil, controlling directors and shareholders are jointly and severally liable for reassessed tax, statutory interest, and penalties; cross-border mutual assistance in recovery permits attachment of personal assets and travel bans in both the foreign jurisdiction and Samoa.
